YOGA-2019JUN-P2-Q90.question_text: Shatkarma, asana, pranayama and meditation are important means of maintaining which of the following?
YOGA-2019JUN-P2-Q90.passage: Yoga is the science of holistic living, and it means 'to join'. In the spiritual world this joining is explained as the union of individual consciousness with universal consciousness. On the practical level, yoga is a means of establishing balance and harmony in body, mind and emotions. It works on the holistic principles of harmony and oneness. It affects every aspect of the personality: physical, mental, social, emotional and spiritual. This can be done through the practice of ashtanga yoga and saptanga yoga. In the twenty-first century, besides the spiritual goal of yoga, physical and mental therapy are among yoga's achievements. Yoga has succeeded as a therapy for controlling various diseases. Yoga therapy succeeds in establishing balance in the nervous and endocrine systems, which has a direct effect on all the organs of the body. Research is currently being done on the effects of yoga practice during and after work. Its results show that shatkarma, asana, pranayama, meditation and so on are important means of maintaining physical and mental health. In view of these facts, millions of people in India and abroad practise yoga every day and take part in the International Day of Yoga, celebrated every year on 21 June. A Common Yoga Protocol has been prepared to spread awareness among people and communities for achieving harmony, peace and freedom from disease.

YOGA-2019JUN-P2-Q96.question_text: Which of the following kleshas belong to the domain of the intellect?
YOGA-2019JUN-P2-Q96.passage: According to Maharshi Patanjali, the five kleshas that disturb the equilibrium of consciousness are avidya, asmita, raga, dvesha and abhinivesha. Lack of true knowledge is the source of all suffering, whether the kleshas are dormant, attenuated, interrupted or fully active. Avidya is the mother of all the kleshas. The body and the self are different, but because of asmita a person feels them to be one. Pleasant experiences give rise to desire and emotional attachment. Unhappiness results in hatred and a sense of insignificance. Clinging to life, or the fear of death, is inherent in all human beings, and even the wise are not free of it. These five kleshas work at three levels: intellectual, emotional and instinctive. Avidya and asmita belong to the domain of the intellect. Raga and dvesha relate to emotions and feelings. The tendency of the klesha abhinivesha is instinctive. The root causes of these five kleshas are behavioural functioning and thinking. The processes of thought and action have existed since the beginning of civilisation, and humans have always been searching for true knowledge. In the context of sadhana, the discriminating power of the intellect finally turns into pure wisdom (prajna), which is eternal. A true seeker is able, through yoga, to destroy the kleshas at their very beginning.
